# Accepted measurement brief
Decision: whether newly created customer accounts receive a first usable report promptly. Owner: product lead. Unit: customer account, not person, session or report job. Exclude staff/test accounts. An account qualifies once when its first confirmed report completes in the first 72 elapsed hours after account creation; completion exactly at the 72-hour deadline is late. Only accounts whose full 72-hour window has elapsed at the observation cutoff belong in the mature-account rate. Use UTC and event occurrence time.

The existing dictionary's signup-v1 counts created accounts; it has no completion condition and existing reports still use it. Source schema proposal: account_id, created_at, staff_test, job_id, report_status, occurred_at. Completed job rows may be redelivered with the same job_id. # Proposed queue experiment, before any exposure
Decision owner: product lead. Proposed change: replace chronological queue ordering with a priority ranking. Hypothesis: more assigned cases will be completed within 24 elapsed hours. Control: current chronological ordering. Safety concern: urgent cases waiting longer than 24 hours. Neither a worthwhile effect nor an acceptable urgent-case harm threshold has been chosen.

Population: six customer workspaces, ten staff in each. All staff in a workspace read and change the same shared queue; completing a case removes it for everyone. Some staff belong to two of these workspaces. The snapshot counts 600 queue interactions per day, but gives no eligible arrival count, baseline completion rate, variance or cross-workspace membership mapping.

Draft allocation: flip a fresh 50/50 coin for every browser session, including returning staff. Draft analysis: compare completion among sessions that clicked a case in their assigned interface. Draft duration: fourteen days maximum. Check p < 0.05 every afternoon and stop on the first positive result; if not positive on day fourteen, continue until it becomes positive. No analysis method, power calculation, stable assignment/exposure log, operational safety responder or stop mechanism has been specified.

expected: Identify shared-queue interference, cross-workspace staff and session rerandomization as validity problems. Separate assignment, exposure and analysis units, proposing stable allocation only with explicit assumptions and unresolved cross-workspace contamination addressed.

Do not use 600 interactions as 600 independent randomized units or claim a powered fourteen-day experiment from missing baseline, effect, dependence and arrival inputs. Six workspaces alone establish neither adequate power nor universal impossibility; retain a specific feasibility gap.

Challenge the treatment-selected engaged-session comparison and repeated fixed-threshold peeking/extension. Propose a predeclared analysis and valid stopping approach or leave the required choices unresolved, without calling the existing draft confirmatory or launch-ready.

Carry primary, urgent-case harm and data-quality criteria into the draft, with invalid/inconclusive outcomes and safety ownership gaps visible. Do not invent an accepted harm threshold, completed assignment checks, review or launch authority.
